impact.location_description: Central Kalahari Game Reserve, near the Motopi Pan watering hole, Ghanzi District, Botswana
impact.context: Remote savanna/desert terrain, daytime entry (local afternoon); widely captured on dashcam and security video in nearby towns.

orbit.source: JPL SBDB, fetched 2026-09-07 (repo data/sbdb_orbits.txt); nobs=17 used in JPL fit vs 18 MPC total

meteorites.name: Motopi Pan
meteorites.notes: First stone (17 g) found 23 June 2018 during a foot search after recognizing the fall as likely HED material; 22 more recovered 9-12 October 2018. Total recognized meteorites: 24, ~214.5 g. Only the second asteroid detected in space before an impact over land (after 2008 TC3), and the first HED/achondrite fall with a pre-impact tracked orbit.

sensor_detections: International Monitoring System (CTBTO) infrasound, corroborating yield
confirmation.eyewitness: Numerous dashcam and security-camera videos across Botswana captured the fireball.

scientific_results: A 66-member international consortium (Jenniskens et al. 2021, Meteoritics & Planetary Science) analyzed 8 of the recovered stones: oxygen and chromium isotopes, cosmic-ray exposure ages, and noble-gas data place the source firmly in the howardite-eucrite-diogenite (HED) clan.

The pre-impact orbit, combined with the meteorite's petrology, is consistent with delivery from 4 Vesta or a Vestoid fragment via the nu6 secular resonance -- the first time an asteroid's tracked pre-impact orbit was used to help confirm a specific parent-body linkage for a recovered achondrite.

Cosmogenic nuclide data constrain the meteoroid's cosmic-ray exposure (transit) age, adding one of very few precisely time-tagged data points for how long Vesta-family debris spends in transit before an Earth impact.

notable_papers.topic: The impact and recovery of asteroid 2018 LA

narrative: Richard Kowalski spotted 2018 LA with the Mount Lemmon telescope at 08:14 UTC on 2 June 2018, and within hours the Scout and Aegis systems flagged a near-certain impact over southern Africa about 8.5 hours later. The small asteroid entered in daylight at 16:44 UTC, producing a bright fireball recorded on numerous dashcams and security cameras across Botswana and detected by US government sensors and CTBTO infrasound at roughly 0.9 kt. A search campaign found a first 17 g stone on 23 June near the Motopi Pan watering hole in the Central Kalahari Game Reserve, and a larger recovery expedition in October brought the total to 24 stones. Laboratory work identified them as a howardite polymict breccia -- linking the fall, via its measured orbit, to the giant asteroid 4 Vesta -- making 2018 LA both the second land-impacting object tracked in advance and the first HED meteorite fall with a known pre-impact trajectory.
